acme-customer: We're seeing intermittent JSON parse failures coming from structured/json mode when file paths contain backslashes and a combining accent. Happens only when we use streaming responses. Parser reports: 'Unexpected end of JSON input'

acme-customer: Minimal repro: POST /v1/responses with model=redwood-fast, mode=structured, stream=true. SDK v1.4.2. Token redacted.

jess-support: Thanks — can you paste the raw streaming payload (the exact bytes you receive, not what the SDK gives you)? That helps us see chunk boundaries.

acme-customer: Pasted raw stream below (we sanitized other fields). Notice the chunk boundary splits an escape sequence and a combining diacritic:

```
data: {"id":"r1","delta":"{\"file_path\":\"C:\\Users\\Jo"
data: {"id":"r1","delta":"n\u0301\\Documents\\report.txt","status":"ok"}"}
```

acme-customer: When the client concats chunks naively the joined string becomes invalid because the backslash runs across the chunk boundary and the combining char sequence separates the base char, our JSON parser fails.

sam-runtime: This looks like a classic streaming-fragment escape issue. The server is emitting escaped JSON, but the chunker is slicing inside a multi-byte/escape sequence so the client sees an incomplete escape like `\\Jo` + `n\u0301` instead of `\\Jón`.

sam-runtime: Quick workaround: switch to non-streaming (stream=false) for that endpoint and you'll get one atomic JSON payload. Also try upgrading the SDK to v1.4.3 — we shipped a streaming-frag fix last week that performs atomic JSON frame assembly client-side.

acme-customer: Can you confirm whether this is a server-side regression? We only started seeing it after the 2026-03 runtime rollout. Latency went up too around the same time.

deploy-bot: @channel deploy: runtime/streaming-chunker rolled to prod in us-east-1 at 2026-03-02T09:02:13Z by @engops. Change: updated chunking heuristic to reduce network overhead.

aron-cs: Escalating to oncall and eng runtime. Filed internal ticket INF-7892 with the raw stream bytes and customer logs.

sam-runtime: Thanks @aron-cs. I'll pull logs for the specific request ids you supplied and run a reproducer locally. If it's the chunking heuristic we'll either back out the change or add guard logic to avoid slicing inside escape sequences / combining-char boundaries.

jess-support: For the customer: temporary mitigation steps — 1) set stream=false in your request, 2) upgrade SDK to v1.4.3 (adds atomic frame reassembly), 3) if you must stream, add a small client-side buffer to accumulate until you detect a closing `\"`/`}` before parsing.

acme-customer: We'll try non-streaming for now and test SDK v1.4.3. Please keep us posted on the rollback or patch ETA, this blocks our ingest pipeline.

sam-runtime: Will update here once we have logs. If we confirm a regression we'll aim for either a targeted rollback in us-east-1 or a server patch within 24 hours. Appreciate the repro, that made it easy to see the cut point. :thumbsup:

acme-customer: Thanks all — attaching a small capture of our parser error and request ids in INF-7892.
